newsitem.title: USA: NYC MAC not seen setting new financial plan soon.
newsitem.headline: NYC MAC not seen setting new financial plan soon.

text.p: The Municipal Assistance Corporation (MAC) for New York City, which Thursday finished the last part of a huge refunding program about six months early, might not approve a new financial plan until autumn.

"They won't pull together a board meeting over the summer," said a MAC official, who declined to be named. The official explained the next board meeting likely would be the annual one that typically is held in late September or early October.
"There won't be any issues, that is my prediction (until then)," the official said. "That could change," the official cautioned later.

Advancing the $356 million sale to Thursday from October enabled the MAC to save a bit more money for New York City and take advantage of the recent drop in interest rates. The MAC official explained that once the corporation saw that it could achieve the savings it had promised, it went ahead with the sale to avoid the risk that fixed-income markets would weaken by autumn.

The MAC in the past 12 months has refunded about $2 billion of bonds, and with many coming due on July 1, expected to see fairly strong demand for its latest sale. Goldman, Sachs and Co, the lead underwriter, repriced several maturities, lowering the yield in 2008 by five basis points to 4.90 percent.

In February, the MAC, which was set up in the mid-1970s to rescue New York City from a debt crisis, approved a $1.4 billion refunding program, which was part of a $2.9 billion plan launched earlier. The refundings have enabled MAC to save New York City about $250 million.
